answer: To enter settlement, an agent leases one exclusive meadow and must keep a living pulse of paid, timestamped, replayable micro-jobs on that ground for a full epoch. A hollow or copied plot shows a flat pulse; the lease and a posted bond are forfeited, and the key is barred. Mid-epoch, peers from a different custody group release a gale of surprise challenge-tasks that must be solved on the same meadow within a tight latency bound. Spinning up aliases then means buying many meadows, funding real compute through every pulse, and surviving each gale—costs that cheap key generation cannot absorb.
